newsitem.title: USA: U.S. jobless claims rose in latest week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. jobless claims rose in latest week.

text.p: U.S. Labor Department report of initial state jobless benefit claims, seasonally adjusted.
Week Ended Initial Claims 4-Week Avg. Continued Claims

R-Revised, Feb 8 Initial Claims from 309,000 and Jan 25 from 337,000; Feb 8 Four-Week Average from 327,750, Feb 1 from 330,750 and Jan 25 from 341,250; Feb 1 Continued Claims from 2,432,000 and Jan 25 from 2,450,000.
Wall Street economists had forecast initial jobless claims of 323,000 in the February 15 week.
The report included the department's annual revisions to seasonal factors, which affect data going back to 1984.
The four-week moving average for the week ended February 15 was at its lowest level since the week ended August 17, 1996 when it stood at 315,500, the department said.
The department said five states reported decreases in claims exceeding 1,000 on an unadjusted basis in the week ended February 8, the latest period for which data are available.
They were Pennsylvania, with 2,979 fewer jobless claims, Ohio with 2,506, Iowa with 1,389, New Mexico with 1,172 and Illinois with 1,108.
Pennsylvania reported fewer layoffs in the food, lumber, furniture and electrical equipment industries. Ohio and Iowa gave no reason for the drop in claims.
New Mexico said it had fewer layoffs in the construction, trade, service and mining industries. Illinois reported fewer layoffs in the construction, trade and service industries.
Labor said three states reported increases in initial claims exceeding 1,000, unadjusted, in the February 8 week.
They were California, with 5,579 additional claims filings, North Carolina with 2,032 and Texas with 1,278.
California said it had layoffs in agriculture. North Carolina gave no explanation for its increase, while Texas reported layoffs in the service, food and furniture industries.
